messages.subject: Multilevel mediation (1-1-1) with missing data
parts:
Dear community,

I intend to do a multilevel mediation and I am struggling with the interpretation.
I have individuals measured on multiple occasions, so my data is clustered by individuals ("ID").
I have three independent variables (IV1, IV2, IV3), that predict an outcome variable (DV), which is mediated by a mediator (Med).
All variables are measured on level 1. I want to model the mediation on level 1 (1-1-1 meditation). The model can be seen below.

I am wondering if I have to interpret the regression output for level 1 or level 2?

The other tricky part is, I have a lot of missings on the IVs because at every measurment occasion, only 1 of the 3 IVs was measured. That's why I used FIML for the missing data. Is this a good idea or are there any better suggestions?

Here is my model:

mod <- '

level:1
DV ~ e*Med + f1*IV1 + f2*IV2 + f3*IV3
Med ~ d1*IV1 + d2*IV2+ d3*IV3

level:2
DV ~ b*Med + c1*IV1 + c2*IV2 + c3*IV3
Med ~ a1*IV1 + a2*IV2+ a3*IV3

IV1~~ IV1
IV2~~ IV2
IV3 ~~ IV3

#between
ab:=a1*b + a2*b + a3*b
totalbw:=ab+c1+c2+c3
#within
de:= d1*e + d2*e + d3*e
totalwith:= de + f1 + f2 + f3'

fit_mod<- sem(mod, data=df, cluster="ID", missing = "fiml", fixed.x = FALSE)
summary(fit_mod, fit.measures=TRUE)

I very much appreciate any help and comments. Thank you!
Kind regards
Eva

messages.author: 4000c7dfaee95484
messages.subject: Re: Multilevel mediation (1-1-1) with missing data
parts:
Hi Eva,

Regarding interpreting either level 1 or level 2 would depend on your research question. With the multi-level model you get both between and within effects, I think both are important to interpret as they could have different implications for your research. But again, it all depends on your aim for the analysis.

Another alternative to FIML would be to use multiple implementation, I would recommend using the mice package for this.
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mice/mice.pdf

However, perhaps you could elaborate one why one of three variables were measured at each time point. 

Best,
Emily Vira
